messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran a week of synthetic warmup experiments against staging to test different prewarm strategies (deploy-time, autoscaler-trigger, and scheduled synthetic traffic). Putting raw notes here, want quick opinions on safety and ops costs before we push to prod.

maria: Nice. Do we have hit-rate deltas? numbers matter for the cost analysis.

alex: Short summary: deploy-time warmers (one-off per rollout) -> ~42% increase in prefix hit-rate for first 30s, autoscaler-trigger micro-warmers -> ~28% hit-rate uplift during scale-ups, scheduled low-qps synthetic -> small steady uplift ~12% but continuous cost. Full numbers below.

cheng: Can you paste the profiling traces? curious about KV cache churn / eviction patterns.

alex: Pasted a couple snippets. Key observations: warmers reduce KV lookups by ~35% in first-token latency path; however, we saw a regression when the warmer payloads didn't match exactly the production prefix tokenization (whitespace/normalization) -> cache misses. We need canonical keying.

alex: Example (debug log):
```
[2026-01-23T14:05:12Z] warmup: sent synthetic req id=wm-8242 prefix="Hello, can you" model=redwood-3b quant=8k
[2026-01-23T14:05:12Z] cache: miss key=sha256("Hello, can you")
[2026-01-23T14:05:12Z] serve: compute kernel=a100-opt v=1.9
[2026-01-23T14:05:12Z] perf: first_token_latency=312ms
```

cheng: That key mismatch is the killer. We should canonicalize the prefix exactly the same way the runtime does (strip, normalize unicode, apply byte-pair tokenization) before we hash. Otherwise warmers are lying to us.

sasha: +1 on canonicalization. For scheduled warmers, also suggest sharding by model-variant and region to avoid cross-variant pollution. Might be obvious but saw it bite us last quarter.

ryan: Cost note: scheduled synthetic at even 5rps across 50 regions is $$$. We need budget caps and an opt-in per-customer setting for Dedicated customers. Also rate-limit warmers to avoid autoscaler thrashing.

alex: Agreed. Proposal for a layered approach:
- deploy-time: deterministic set of canonical prefixes derived from top-k recent prompts for the service + a few coverage tokens (zero-cost if we integrate with rollout hooks)
- autoscaler-trigger: on an up-scale event, emit micro-warmers targeted at the most-likely prefixes for that hour (based on sliding 1h histogram)
- scheduled: very low qps background sweep focusing only on coldest shards / long-tail prefixes
- simulated user traffic: only for canary tenants, flagged and logged separately

maria: How do we pick prefixes? public fallback set vs service-specific. Also how do we avoid sensitive data in warmers?

alex: Prefix selection: two sources — public canonical seed list (for generic models) + sliding-window top-K (K=100) per-service derived from anonymized token n-grams. We will scrub PII at generation: strip emails, phone numbers, long GUIDs; and hash the payloads before persistent storage. Warmers sent to model will still be plaintext but scrubbed.

perf-bot: [alert] regression detected: median first_token_latency increased from 210ms -> 260ms on candidate/feature/warmers-v3 at 2026-02-01T03:12:01Z. Traces: https://internal.perf/redwood/compare/feat-warmers-v2..v3

cheng: I pulled the trace — that regression correlates with a kernel selection change for long-prefix paths. When warmers increased cache occupancy, the kernel selector started preferring an attention kernel that has worse cold-start JIT time but better steady-state throughput. Warmers amplify cold-starts in the short-window case.

sasha: So warmers improved hit-rate but shifted the serving runtime into kernel choices that penalize very short-lived instances. That's subtle. Maybe we need to include a warmers-aware flag in kernel selection that considers recent warmup calls when deciding JIT thresholds.

alex: Idea: add a warmup_score per shard (ephemeral metric) that influences kernel selection. If warmup_score > threshold then prefer kernels with higher JIT but better steady throughput; else prefer low-JIT kernels. This avoids the regression on ephemeral warmers.

ryan: We should also ensure warmers are idempotent and can be marked with metadata so billing and observability treat them differently. Eg headers: `X-Warmup: 1`, `X-Source: deploy-warner`.

alex: Example warmup curl (for deploy hook):
```
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMER_KEY" \
  -H "X-Warmup: 1" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"Hello, can you summarize"}'
```

maria: How about instrumentation? what metrics to add?

cheng: Minimum: `cache.prefix_hits`, `cache.prefix_misses`, `warmers.sent_total`, `warmers.success_total`, `warmers.cost_estimate_usd`, plus `kernel.selector.choice_count{kernel=...}` and `first_token_latency_by_warmup_flag`. Also tracking `cache.key_entropy` (unique keys per minute) to detect pollution.

sasha: For scheduled jobs, here's a tiny k8s CronJob YAML for the sweeper (draft):
```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: prefix-warm-sweeper
spec:
  schedule: "*/30 * * * *" # every 30 minutes, very conservative
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: sweeper
            image: internal/warmers:stable
            args: ["--shard=auto","--limit=20","--rate=0.5"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

ryan: Remember RBAC and key rotation on those images. Also make the CronJob namespace-scoped per-team so we don't leak keys.

alex: Next steps I'm proposing:
1) implement canonical keying in warmers generator (normalize + tokenize + sha256) — cheng/ops to pair on this
2) add `X-Warmup` header support and metrics `warmers.*` — eng-runtime and observability
3) kernel selector change to consider warmup_score — perf/eng-runtime prototype
4) implement shard-aware scheduled sweeper (rate-limited) and opt-in flags for Dedicated customers
5) run a staged rollouts: canary tenant -> staging prod -> all prod with budget guardrails

maria: +1. can we get a rough cost estimate for step 4? I'll model it against current infra rates.

cheng: I'll start a PR for canonical keying and a small synthetic generator that mirrors runtime tokenization. Will link when ready.

alex: thanks. I'll open a short RFC with the above plan and link tests/benchmarks. If anyone has objections to the rollout plan or sees a missing failure mode call it out now. :thumbsup:

sasha: minor: add fail-open behavior if warmers are rejected by quota or rate-limiting so real traffic isn't affected.

ryan: noted. Also add cost alarm if `warmers.cost_estimate_usd > $50/day` per-org.

alex: great, closing thread. PRs incoming.
